arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-01.question: Your employer wants to charge employees for the cost of new protective gloves they are required to wear. Is this allowed?

options.a: Yes, as long as the cost is calculated proportionally and transparently
options.b: Yes, if the works council agrees
options.c: No, the law does not allow the employer to pass the cost of occupational safety measures on to employees
options.d: No, unless the gloves cost more than 20 euros each

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-01.explanation: The German Occupational Safety Act makes clear that protective equipment and other safety measures are the employer's responsibility, including financially. Employees may not be charged for measures meant to protect their own safety and health at work - regardless of the price or whether the works council agrees.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-02.question: A colleague finds the mandatory safety goggles at the workbench annoying and prefers to work without them. How does this stand under employees' legal duties?

options.a: Not a problem, as long as nothing has happened so far
options.b: He is violating his legal duty to properly use the personal protective equipment made available to him
options.c: That is solely the concern of the safety officer, not of the employee themselves
options.d: It is acceptable because only the employer is responsible for provision, not for use

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-02.explanation: Employees are legally required to properly use machines, tools, protective devices, and the personal protective equipment provided to them. The employer must supply the PPE, but using it correctly day to day is each individual's own responsibility - and that is exactly what protects your eyes in an actual accident.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-03.question: A strong smell of gas suddenly fills the production hall and an alarm sounds - an immediate serious danger. What applies to employees in this situation?

options.a: They may leave the workplace immediately to bring themselves to safety, and this may not be held against them in any way
options.b: They must first get their supervisor's permission before leaving the workplace
options.c: They may only leave the workplace if the works fire brigade explicitly orders it
options.d: Leaving is only legally protected once a fire has actually broken out, not merely at the smell of gas

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-03.explanation: German occupational safety law explicitly gives employees the right, in the face of immediate serious danger to safety and health, to bring themselves to safety by leaving the workplace at once - without needing prior permission and without this being held against them. The employer must in fact make this possible in the first place, for example through working escape routes and an alarm system.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-04.question: In a warehouse, one area is loud because a machine is running without any sound insulation. Which order of measures matches the general principles of occupational safety?

options.a: Immediately issue hearing protection to everyone; technical changes to the machine are a secondary concern
options.b: Only relocate the employees most affected, leaving everything else unchanged
options.c: Wait and see if anyone complains about the noise before doing anything at all
options.d: First check whether the noise can be reduced technically at the source (e.g. enclosing the machine); only use personal protective equipment like ear protection if that is not enough

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-04.explanation: The general principles of occupational safety require hazards to be tackled at their source wherever possible, with individual protective measures like personal protective equipment used only as a last resort, once technical and organizational measures cannot sufficiently eliminate the risk. Hearing protection is therefore not the first line of defense, but the last.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-01.question: A new colleague in her department is assigned a new machine she has never worked on before. By when must an instruction on this be given at the latest?

options.a: Only after the six-month probationary period ends
options.b: Before the new machine is used for the first time, tailored to this specific workstation and the new equipment
options.c: Only once the annual department-wide group instruction session is due
options.d: Only if there has already been an accident involving similar machines

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-01.explanation: The duty to instruct employees is not limited to the start of employment - it explicitly also applies whenever job duties change or new equipment or technology is introduced. Before someone uses a new piece of equipment for the first time, they must receive instruction tailored to that specific workstation, regardless of any probation period or the annual schedule.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-02.question: A company held its last general safety instruction exactly 13 months ago, and nothing about the tasks, equipment, or hazards has changed since. Does this meet the requirements?

options.a: Yes, since nothing about the tasks has changed since the last instruction, no new one is needed
options.b: Yes, because a repeat instruction is only required after a workplace accident
options.c: No, the repeat instruction must happen at least once a year regardless of whether anything changed - the deadline has already passed here
options.d: No, but it is sufficient to catch up on the instruction within the next two years

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-02.explanation: In addition to the trigger-based requirement (new tasks, new equipment, new hazards), the relevant accident-prevention regulation sets a fixed minimum frequency: instruction must be repeated as needed, but at least once a year. An unchanged workplace does not exempt anyone from this annual repetition.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-03.question: What is the employer required to do after carrying out a safety instruction session?

options.a: Document the content and date of the instruction, so that compliance with the duty can be proven afterwards
options.b: Nothing further - a purely verbal instruction with no record at all is always sufficient on its own
options.c: Have the instruction session notarized
options.d: It is enough that the instruction took place, regardless of whether it can later be established who attended

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-03.explanation: Instruction must be documented so that, in a dispute or during an inspection - for example after an accident or an authority check - it can be proven who was instructed on what topic and when. No formal notarization is required; a simple instruction record signed by the attendee is the common approach.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-04.question: A company assigns a temporary agency worker and an intern to production work for two weeks. Do both of them also need to receive workplace-specific safety instruction?

options.a: No, the duty to instruct only applies to permanent, full-time employees
options.b: Yes, the duty to instruct applies to everyone deployed in the workplace, regardless of contract type or duration - for the agency worker, this duty falls on the host company using their labor
options.c: No, for agency workers only the staffing agency remains responsible; the host company has no duty at all
options.d: Yes, but only the intern needs to be instructed; an exception applies to agency workers

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-04.explanation: The definition of "employee" under German occupational safety law is broad and explicitly includes interns and temporary agency workers. For agency work, the duty to give workplace-specific instruction rests with the company that actually deploys the worker (the host company) - the staffing agency's separate general duties remain in place but do not substitute for this.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: What is the basic purpose of the risk assessment (Gefährdungsbeurteilung) under German occupational safety law?

options.a: A purely formal document for the accident insurer with no real practical effect on daily work
options.b: A one-time stocktake that is only needed when a company is founded
options.c: The systematic identification of hazards connected with the work, in order to determine which occupational safety measures are actually necessary
options.d: An assessment that exclusively covers psychological strain in the workplace

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: The employer must determine which protective measures are necessary by assessing the hazards connected with the work. This is not a one-off administrative box-tick, but the technical basis for concrete decisions - from choosing machinery to organizing work to selecting PPE. Psychological strain is just one of several factors to be considered, not the sole subject of the assessment.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: Which of the following statements about possible causes of hazards under German occupational safety law is NOT correct?

options.a: The design and setup of workplaces and work premises can constitute a hazard
options.b: Physical, chemical, and biological exposures count among possible sources of hazard
options.c: Psychological strain at work must also be considered as a possible hazard
options.d: Only directly visible technical defects in machinery count as a hazard; organizational aspects such as work processes play no role

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: The law explicitly lists several sources of hazard, including workplace design, physical/chemical/biological exposures, the design of work equipment, work processes and working hours, insufficient qualification, and psychological strain. Organizational factors such as work processes are explicitly included, not excluded.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: An employee notices an obvious defect in a safety guard that constitutes an immediate serious danger. How should they behave under the law?

options.a: Wait until the next scheduled safety inspection and raise the defect then
options.b: They are required to report the defect to the employer or the responsible supervisor without delay
options.c: Repair the defect themselves to save time, even without the appropriate qualification
options.d: Ignore the incident, as long as the machine still outwardly appears to work normally despite the defect

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: Employees have a specific duty to report: any immediate serious danger to safety and health they identify, as well as any defect they find in protective systems, must be reported without delay. Fixing it themselves without the right qualification, or waiting for the next routine inspection, both conflict with this duty and can prolong the danger for everyone involved.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: A warehouse introduces a new, significantly faster picking system using driverless transport vehicles. What follows for the existing risk assessment?

options.a: It must be reviewed and updated as needed, because the working conditions - and therefore the hazard situation - have changed substantially
options.b: Nothing - the original risk assessment remains valid until a statutory five-year deadline expires
options.c: Nothing - risk assessments only need to be created when a business first opens
options.d: It only needs to be adjusted once an accident involving the new vehicles has already occurred

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: There is no fixed statutory deadline, such as five years, after which a risk assessment automatically expires. Instead, whenever working conditions change substantially - for example through new equipment, new vehicles, or changed processes - the assessment must be reviewed and updated as needed, and this should happen before an accident reveals that it was out of date.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-01.question: You notice that your mandatory hearing protection is damaged and its noise reduction has clearly worsened as a result. How should you respond?

options.a: Keep using it as long as you can still feel some damping material
options.b: Stop using the damaged protective equipment and inform your employer so replacement equipment can be provided
options.c: Improvise yourself with tape to bridge the time until the next order arrives
options.d: Simply swap the damaged hearing protection for a private earplug of unknown origin

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-01.explanation: Personal protective equipment only protects if it actually still works properly. Employees must use the PPE provided to them as intended - continuing to use damaged equipment or improvising a replacement yourself defeats that purpose. A noticed defect in protective equipment should be reported so the employer can arrange a proper replacement.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-02.question: A large moving box has been sitting for several days directly in front of a door marked as an escape route in an office corridor. How should this be assessed?

options.a: Not a problem, as long as the box could quickly be pushed aside if needed
options.b: Acceptable, as long as a second escape route still exists somewhere in the building
options.c: Not acceptable - escape routes and emergency exits must remain fully clear and usable at their full width at all times
options.d: Acceptable, as long as the box is not made of flammable material

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-02.explanation: Escape routes and emergency exits must be kept clear at all times, so that in an emergency - for example fire or smoke - everyone can leave the building quickly and without obstruction. An object blocking an escape door or narrowing the escape route is a safety risk regardless of whether it is flammable, even if a second escape route exists.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-03.question: In an office kitchen, oil in a pan on the stove catches fire. Why is a conventional water fire extinguisher a poor choice here?

options.a: Fires involving fats/oils belong to their own fire class, where water can actually make things worse by causing a fat explosion/fireball - special extinguishing agents are needed instead
options.b: Water extinguishers are generally weaker than every other type of extinguisher and are not suitable for any type of fire
options.c: Water extinguishers may only be used by the fire brigade for insurance reasons
options.d: It does not matter which type of extinguisher is used, as long as it is within reach

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-03.explanation: Fires are classified by the type of burning material, including solids, liquids, gases, metals, and cooking oils/fats. With a burning fat fire, water can trigger a so-called fat explosion, producing a fireball and massively worsening the fire - specially approved fat-fire extinguishers exist for exactly this case. That is why it matters to know which extinguisher type suits which kind of fire.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-04.question: A colleague gets a minor cut on their finger and treats it themselves with a plaster from the first-aid box. They think nobody else needs to know. What is the usual principle for reporting incidents like this?

options.a: Minor injuries generally never need to be reported or documented at all
options.b: Even minor first-aid treatments should be recorded in the first-aid logbook, so that a connection to the work can be traced later if needed
options.c: A report is only required for a hospital stay of more than three days
options.d: Only the works council needs to be informed; no written documentation is intended

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-04.explanation: Even seemingly harmless injuries should be documented, for example in a first-aid logbook, because some consequences only become apparent later, and in a dispute - for instance with the accident insurer - it must be possible to prove that an injury was work-related. This protects the injured person themselves, in case what seemed like a small wound later develops into a more serious complication.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-01.question: An employee works at a screen continuously all day without a break. What does the Workplaces Ordinance (ArbStättV) fundamentally require here?

options.a: A fixed 15-minute break must occur after every full hour of screen work, without exception
options.b: There is no legal requirement whatsoever regarding interruptions during screen work
options.c: Screen work must be interrupted by other activities or recovery periods, with the specific arrangement to be determined as part of the risk assessment
options.d: An interruption is only legally required once daily screen work reaches ten hours

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-01.explanation: The Workplaces Ordinance requires that screen work be interrupted by other activities or recovery periods, but it does not prescribe a rigid schedule like exactly 15 minutes every hour. How the interruptions are actually arranged (mixed tasks, short breaks) is something the employer must determine for the specific workstation as part of the risk assessment.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-02.question: An employee at a typical screen workstation wants to know whether they are entitled to an eye examination. What applies?

options.a: An entitlement only exists once a medically confirmed vision impairment is already present
options.b: The employer must offer him what is called Angebotsvorsorge (offered preventive check-up); participation is voluntary but recommended
options.c: An eye examination is mandatory for every screen workstation and cannot be declined
options.d: An entitlement only exists for employees over the age of 50

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-02.explanation: For screen workstations, what is called Angebotsvorsorge applies: the employer must offer the examination, but the employee is not obliged to take part. In practice, most people do take up the offer, since vision problems caught early are usually easier to treat - neither an already-confirmed vision impairment nor reaching a certain minimum age is a precondition.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-03.question: The eye examination under the offered preventive check-up shows that an employee needs special screen-work glasses because their normal glasses are not sufficient for screen work. Who bears the cost of an appropriate pair of screen-work glasses?

options.a: The employer, provided the need was established through the occupational medical examination and a normal-standard model of glasses is chosen
options.b: The employee, since it is a private vision aid regardless of the reason
options.c: Statutory health insurance automatically covers the full cost of any glasses
options.d: There is no rule on this at all; the cost question is freely negotiable and legally completely open

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-03.explanation: If the occupational medical examination establishes that normal glasses are not sufficient for screen work, the employer must provide or pay for a special pair of screen-work glasses within a reasonable standard. Luxury frames or extras beyond that may fall to the employee, but the necessary basic provision is the employer's responsibility.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-04.question: Which of the following statements about the basic design of a screen workstation is correct?

options.a: Screen height and the distance to the employee play no relevant role for ergonomics
options.b: Glare and reflections on the screen from windows or lighting are irrelevant from an occupational safety standpoint
options.c: Ergonomic design is only required in permanently assigned individual offices, not in open-plan offices
options.d: The workstation should be designed to avoid disruptive glare and reflections, and the screen, keyboard, and seating should enable an ergonomically sound working posture

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-04.explanation: The requirements for screen work include avoiding glare and disruptive reflections on the screen, and designing and arranging the screen, keyboard, and seating so that an ergonomically favorable posture is possible. These requirements apply regardless of whether it is an individual office or an open-plan office.
